transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess I'm here because... I just feel like I'm always moving from one thing to the next. Like I can't really just sit idle. And, uh, we have a new setup at work recently, which... well, it's just made that a lot harder to hide. So, I figured I should come in.
Do you often feel physically restless or fidgety?

Yeah, I suppose. Um... even when I try to look calm, my foot is usually bouncing under the desk. Or... I'll just be clicking a pen in a meeting and not really notice I'm doing it. Just things like that.
Do you often act without thinking?
Um... no, I wouldn't say so. Not that I've noticed, anyway.
Do you often have trouble paying close attention to details or making careless mistakes?

Yeah, I guess so. Um... like at work, with customer tickets. I'll think I've finished one, but then... later I'll notice I typed the wrong account number or something. Or maybe I skipped a required box. Just missing one little instruction, and the whole thing comes back to me. So... yeah, that happens.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot most days?
No... not really. I don't think I worry any more than anyone else. Just normal stuff, I guess.
Do you often interrupt other people or blurt out answers before they finish asking a question?

Um... sometimes, I guess. I don't mean to be rude about it or anything. But... if I hear my coworkers trying to figure out a customer problem, I'll just sort of... jump in. I'll give them the answer before they're done talking, or... before anyone even asked me. So... yeah. Sometimes.
Did these attention and restlessness symptoms start before you were 12 years old?

Yeah, I guess so. Um... it was around long before this job change, anyway. Back in... well, in grade school, my teachers used to write things on my report cards. Like that I was bright, but careless. Or that I talked out of turn... and they always had to remind me to stay with my work. So... yeah. It's been a while.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive/restless presentation, with longstanding symptoms beginning in grade school. He confirmed inattention (careless mistakes, missing details), hyperactivity/restlessness (foot bouncing, pen clicking, inability to sit idle), and mild impulsive interruptions, with onset before age 12 and current work-related impairment. Full criteria for hyperkinetic disorder with prominent hyperactivity-impulsivity are not clearly established, making F90.0 the best fit.
